Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with several days of dysuria and mild lower abdominal cramping; suspected simple urinary tract infection treated with a 3-day antibiotic; advised fluids and follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Burning/pain on urination for a few days; crampy lower abdominal/colic-type pain; symptoms bothersome with urination.
- Associated symptoms: Slight blood in urine earlier today; urine smell described as somewhat unusual; no nausea, vomiting, fever, or back pain.
- Negative findings noted: No dysuria improvement, no reported diarrhea; no high fever reported.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Allergies: Clindamycin – swelling reaction.
- Medications: Over-the-counter bicarbonate previously tried for pain; no regular medications.
- Social history: Student; lives with friends; non-smoker; consumes alcohol on weekends; sexually active with regular partner; uses condoms; last menstrual period ~3 weeks ago; had no prior STD screening noted.

Examination:
- (Not documented in transcript)

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Simple urinary tract infection (UTI)/bladder infection.

Plan:
- Antibiotics: Three-day course of either nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim; one tablet twice daily for three days.
- Hydration: Advise drinking plenty of fluids; cranberry juice may help.
- Follow-up: If not improved by end of the week, return or call for re-evaluation.
- Warning signs: If high fever, back pain, or feeling generally unwell, contact clinic promptly.
- Pregnancy considerations: If pregnancy is possible, consider a pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy if symptoms persist.
- Activity/sexual health: Avoid sexual intercourse while symptoms persist; continue barrier contraception.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs; physical examination findings; urinalysis results; pregnancy test results; full medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: None detected.
- Transcript quality: Some minor inaudible segments and conversational drift; overall sufficient to determine working diagnosis and plan.
